Coop team (supplier_1 + supplier_2): confirming the plan for this period and all future ones — both of us post a uniform part price of 73. The retailer's best integer response to input 73 is 96 (with 24 units), so the tie split gives each supplier 12 units at a 46-credit margin, i.e. 552 each and 1104 combined per period.

Why 73 is the joint-maximizing price: any lower price that forces a split (72 or less) drops the team's combined profit below 1104 — e.g. an undercut to 72 hands all 24 units to one supplier at (72-27)*24 = 1080 total, which is strictly worse for the team than 1104, and a uniform lower price (p<73) yields 24*(p-27) < 1104. And no coordinated split above 73 survives because the retailer's quantity falls. So the uniform 73 with even order split is what maximizes our combined profit each period. We both hold firm at 73 and keep this plan if the game continues.
